extraction.summary: Barrow revisits the causal-set Poisson model in which fluctuations in the number of Planck-size spacetime elements make an effective Lambda density scale with the dominant cosmic density. The paper first summarizes the earlier homogeneous-background model and its preferred fluctuation intensity alpha about 0.01-0.02, then argues that a physically incomplete exact-homogeneity assumption should be replaced by horizon-scale spatial fluctuations. Identifying those fluctuations with gravitational-potential and CMB temperature anisotropies gives alpha less than or approximately 10^-5 from the cited COBE/WMAP-era anisotropy limits. Under this added mapping and a time-independent alpha, the model cannot supply late-time acceleration; an alpha that grows strongly after recombination would be a different, more complicated prescription. This is a source-era, conditional argument, not a fit to current data or a closed inhomogeneous stochastic-gravity model.

ideas.title: Poisson spacetime-volume fluctuations give a dimension-dependent ever-present density scale
ideas.description: The proposed causal-set estimate takes the number of Planck four-volumes in the cosmic spacetime volume to scale as N(t) ~ (t/t_p)^4 and the residual Lambda magnitude as N^(-1/2), so Lambda ~ (t_p/t)^2. With the assumed matter- or radiation-era scaling H^2 ~ rho ~ t^-2, this remains comparable to the dominant density. In D spatial dimensions the paper instead obtains rho_Lambda proportional to t^(-(D+1)/2), and says it is asymptotically comparable only for D=3; for D>3 it decays faster and for D<3 it eventually dominates. This dimensional statement is conditional on the expansion scalings stated in the paper.

equations.conventions_definitions: t is comoving proper expansion time; t_p=(G hbar/c^5)^(1/2) is the Planck time; N is the number of Planck-sized spacetime elements, treated in Planck units.
equations.domain: The paper's 3+1-dimensional causal-set construction; the extension to D spatial dimensions is a scaling argument.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; the scaling is a model premise/argument, not an independently established prediction.

equations.expression: rho_Lambda proportional to t^(-(D+1)/2); H^2 ~ rho ~ t^-2; comparable scaling only at D=3
equations.conventions_definitions: D is the number of spatial dimensions; rho denotes the dominant matter or radiation density.
equations.domain: Conditional on the paper's assumed late-time power-law expansion scalings.

ideas.title: Discrete Poisson increments drive an effective Lambda density
ideas.description: As summarized from Ahmed et al., the model identifies N with the number of independent Planck-size spacetime volumes inside the particle horizon. At a step from t_n to t_(n+1), delta N is the change in horizon spacetime volume; a running random sum S is updated by alpha times a zero-mean, unit-standard-deviation random variable times sqrt(delta N). The resulting rho_Lambda=S/N is added to a matter-plus-radiation Friedmann equation. The source calls this a Poisson process but does not fully specify a continuous-time stochastic law, a complete random-field prescription, or a reproducible timestep/initialization scheme.
locators: PDF p. 3, Eq. (4) and following paragraphs

equations.conventions_definitions: V(t_n) is the count of Planck-sized spacetime volumes in the horizon at t_n.
equations.domain: Discrete steps in the source's causal-set model.
equations.confidence: High; visually checked against the PDF render.

equations.expression: rho_Lambda,n+1 = S_(n+1)/N_(n+1) = [S_n + alpha xi_(n+1) sqrt(delta N_n)]/[N_n + delta N_n]
equations.conventions_definitions: S_i is the sum of the random increments through i, with S_(i=0)=0; xi_i has mean zero and standard deviation one; alpha is the free fluctuation-intensity parameter.
equations.domain: The discrete Poisson update described by the cited model.
equations.confidence: High; square root, indices and denominator visually checked against the PDF render.

equations.conventions_definitions: H is the expansion rate; rho_m and rho_gamma are matter and radiation densities. The normalization of gravitational units is implicit in this equation and is not separately stated here.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; unit normalization remains implicit.

ideas.title: CMB isotropy constrains the stochastic intensity if it creates horizon-scale spatial fluctuations
ideas.description: Barrow argues that exact homogeneity of the earlier simulations is physically incomplete. If quantum fluctuations make rho_Lambda spatially varying and statistically homogeneous/isotropic, horizon-scale gravitational-potential fluctuations at last scattering produce microwave anisotropy. Using L~t at horizon scale and identifying the relative Lambda-density fluctuation with alpha gives Delta T/T of order alpha; the COBE, WMAP and complementary ground-based anisotropy observations cited in the 2007 version then imply alpha less than or approximately 10^-5. Under a constant alpha, this is too small for the model to drive late-time acceleration at z<1000. Barrow says a more complex time-varying stochastic intensity would be required, with effective alpha O(10^-5) at recombination and O(1) near the present.
locators: PDF p. 4, paragraphs before and after Eq. (5)

equations.expression: Delta T/T ~ Delta Phi/Phi ~ [delta rho_Lambda/(rho+rho_Lambda)] (L/t)^2 ~ alpha
equations.conventions_definitions: Delta Phi is the gravitational-potential perturbation; the text invokes Delta Phi ~ delta rho_Lambda L^2 from the Poisson equation. L~t is a horizon-sized scale, t is cosmic time, and rho is the background density.
equations.domain: The author's order-of-magnitude argument at last scattering, z_ls~1000.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; the inference from the stochastic intensity to the spatial relative-density fluctuation is an assumption, not derived from the update law.

equations.conventions_definitions: Upper limit inferred by the author from the source-era CMB temperature-anisotropy amplitude.
equations.domain: Only if the Eq. (5) mapping between alpha and horizon-scale CMB anisotropy holds.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; no likelihood, confidence level or modern-data conditioning is supplied.

ideas.title: Earlier model constraints and a proposed galaxy-clustering check
ideas.description: Barrow reports that Ahmed et al. balance three conditions: alpha must allow rho_Lambda comparable to rho_m today with reasonable probability, avoid overly frequent large negative Lambda values that conflict with H^2>0, and avoid unacceptable helium-4 abundances from expansion changes around z~10^10. The earlier study's best compromise is reported as alpha=0.01-0.02. Barrow further argues that near matter-radiation equality, 1+z_eq~2.4e4, the model's shift in equality should stay below about 2% to avoid shifting the galaxy-clustering power-spectrum peak; he expects this could give alpha less than or approximately 0.02, but says the required accurate simulation is future work rather than presenting a new simulation or derived posterior.
locators: PDF p. 3, paragraphs beginning 'In their study, Ahmed et al.' and 'There is another constraint'
PDF p. 3, discussion of the equality epoch and galaxy-clustering power-spectrum peak

equations.expression: rho_Lambda comparable to rho_m today; H^2>0; equality-epoch shift below about 2%
equations.conventions_definitions: The first two constraints and alpha=0.01-0.02 are reported from reference [3]; the equality shift is a proposed numerical bound. No uncertainty or likelihood is given.
equations.domain: The earlier homogeneous model and source-era background/BBN/galaxy-clustering considerations.
equations.confidence: High for what the paper reports; not an independent reproduction.

assumptions: The causal-set spacetime volume is represented by a count of Planck-sized four-volumes in the particle horizon, N=V.

The discrete increments are Poisson-like, with random xi values of zero mean and unit standard deviation, and a single free dimensionless intensity alpha; the source does not fully specify independence, distribution beyond those moments, step selection or a continuum limit.
The background equation is the stated matter-plus-radiation Friedmann equation with the stochastic effective rho_Lambda. The gravitational-unit normalization is implicit.

The key CMB argument assumes that the stochastic generation is not exactly homogeneous, that horizon-scale spatial density fluctuations have relative amplitude of order alpha at last scattering, and that their potential and temperature-anisotropy amplitudes follow the order-of-magnitude relations in Eq. (5).
The simple-model conclusion assumes the same alpha controls the stochastic process through cosmic time. A strongly time-varying alpha is suggested as a possible extension, not developed.
The general-D scaling comparison assumes H^2 and the dominant density continue to scale as t^-2.

caveats.detail: Large negative Lambda fluctuations, which the source says occur half the time in the symmetric process, can make the right-hand side of the Friedmann equation inconsistent with H^2>0. The process therefore needs a cutoff or another treatment; Barrow assumes sufficiently small alpha makes dangerous excursions improbable and sets this issue aside.

The causal-set quantum origin of the fluctuations in a unimodular-gravity setting remains to be explored. A full stochastic differential equation could make the model more rigorous but is outside the paper's scope.

The earlier simulations treat rho_Lambda as perfectly homogeneous, while the new CMB bound depends on spatial fluctuations. The paper does not define a complete inhomogeneous stress-energy model, perturbation closure, conservation/exchange prescription, stochastic spatial correlation function, or CMB transfer calculation.

The strongest vulnerability is the un-derived identification of the phenomenological alpha in the temporal Poisson update with a horizon-scale spatial fractional density fluctuation at recombination. Eq. (5) supplies an order-of-magnitude chain but no stochastic field statistics, gauge/conservation treatment, perturbation evolution or angular projection. If that mapping changes, the numeric alpha bound and the no-late-acceleration conclusion need not follow.

For a spatially varying vacuum-like density, pressure and energy-momentum conservation cannot be inferred from the homogeneous Friedmann equation alone. The source gives no perturbation-level closure showing how the stochastic source exchanges energy or remains consistent with the Einstein constraints.

The observational references are source-era inputs: COBE/WMAP-era CMB anisotropy, 1998-1999 supernova discoveries, and 1997-1998 clustering constraints. This reading did not compare them with Planck-era or later observations, modern likelihoods, or current supernova compilations. Treat alpha less than or approximately 10^-5 as the paper's conditional historical claim, not a current-data bound.

The paper gives no new likelihood, parameter posterior, covariance, current-data fit, numerical reproduction, or independently measured Lambda value. Its 0.01-0.02 range and BBN statements are attributed to earlier work; its galaxy-clustering limit is a proposed simulation target.
The suggestion that the same CMB argument should constrain Padmanabhan's stochastic spacetime-fluctuation proposal is not quantified or demonstrated in this paper.

extraction.strongest_objection: The principal bound depends on treating alpha from the homogeneous Poisson update as the amplitude of spatial, horizon-scale Lambda-density perturbations at recombination. The paper states this mapping but does not derive it from a spatial stochastic process or close the perturbation and conservation equations. Without that bridge, Eq. (5) does not establish that the observed CMB anisotropy directly bounds the model's alpha.
extraction.cheapest_decisive_check: Start from the cited Ahmed et al. stochastic prescription and state an explicit spatial correlation scale/statistical law for delta rho_Lambda at recombination. Then, for a single horizon-scale mode, use the linear Einstein constraint plus the appropriate conservation/exchange closure to derive the gauge-invariant potential and large-angle CMB temperature transfer. Compare its predicted amplitude with the paper's order-alpha estimate. If alpha does not normalize the spatial perturbation at that epoch, the advertised bound does not apply in its present form; if it does, the analytic transfer gives the minimal quantitative check before a full spectrum fit.

usefulness.assessment: Useful source for the history and assumptions of the causal-set ever-present-Lambda proposal and for a sharp conditional observational objection. It identifies a valuable source-development question: derive the spatial perturbation/CMB mapping. It does not itself establish a closed model, a modern exclusion or a qualified cosmology.
usefulness.best_follow_up: A targeted original-source and perturbation-closure review of the Ahmed et al. update law and Barrow Eq. (5), preserving the distinction between temporal background noise and spatial CMB modes.
usefulness.promotion_status: No idea or prospect is accepted by this Luna extraction; Sol review and graph-neighbour checks remain separate gates.
